design.title: Canonical-composite reconstruction: each member's 8x8 feature map must repaint the per-pixel MEDIAN of the three training surveys (a picture of Berlin in which anything seen in only one survey is gone), through a training-only decoder that never flies
design.eli5: Three aerial photographs of the same Berlin street disagree about the parked cars, the shadows and the leaves on the trees, but they agree about the roads, the canals and the building footprints. We make a fourth picture of the whole city by majority vote, pixel by pixel: anything that appears in only one photograph simply vanishes, and what two or three agree on stays. During training, the two navigators are shown one real photograph of a place and asked to sketch, in coarse strokes, what that majority-vote picture of the place looks like. The only way to pass the sketching test is to notice the permanent features and ignore the fleeting ones, which is exactly the habit a navigator needs when the drone's own camera takes a fifth photograph nobody has. The sketching pad is thrown away before the model flies; only the habit stays.
design.hypothesis: Nine experiments on this ruler leave the held-out 2024 photograph at 7.5% usable / 17% false fix (exp 7, 1.096) with usable never outside 7-12.5%, and they say, read together, that the deployed feature of a place is still built from survey-specific content: exp 5 lifted the TRAINING photographs to 72-81% usable at the same held-out viewpoints and 2024 did not move (12.5%), so the trunk learns three survey-specific layouts; exp 4's photometric randomisation (the only mechanism that ever moved 2024 accuracy, 7% -> 11.75%) removed the GLOBAL part of a survey change, and the remaining part is CONTENT - shadows of a different sun, parked cars, construction, canopy state, true-ortho artefacts - which no per-view photometric draw can synthesise. Three attempts to make the feature survey-invariant through the three surveys themselves did not get a fair test: exp 3's cosine term was vacuous on non-negative GAP features (0.966 at epoch 1), exp 9's batch-standardised within-place variance penalty at weight 10 destroyed training outright (train top1 0.008 after 8 epochs, member 0 collapsed to a constant answer, xsurvey_agree 0.74 at top1 0.0003 - a training collapse, NOT a verdict on invariance; it is recorded here so it is not read as one), and exp 8's external teacher gave the student a target it could not reach (student-teacher cosine 0.40 against the 0.55 needed; the teacher's own cross-survey cosine was only 0.46-0.53). The common failure is the TARGET: a latent-consistency target can be satisfied for free or collapse, and a 22M-parameter teacher's semantics are not representable by a 1M-parameter CNN. This experiment gives the trunk a target that is survey-invariant BY CONSTRUCTION, cannot collapse, cannot be satisfied for free, and is trivially representable: the per-pixel median of the three training captures after per-survey global colour normalisation. The captures are pixel-aligned on one grid (<= 1 px), so at every pixel the median keeps the value two or three surveys agree on and discards whatever is unique to one photograph: a car, that survey's shadow where the other two are lit, one season's canopy, one year's construction, the leaning roof of the standard DOP against the two true orthos. Design-stage probe on the three TRAINING captures only (runs/_probe_exp10_canon.py, 300 random lattice places at random headings, 4 m/px standardised crops; truedop_2024 never opened): two real surveys of the same place correlate 0.575-0.622 with each other, while each survey correlates 0.812-0.851 with the composite - the composite is the picture the three photographs have in common, and it is much closer to every one of them than they are to each other, so a view from ANY survey can be asked to produce it; nearest-neighbour retrieval over the 300 places from one survey to the composite is 96-100% when aligned (and 12-20% under the eval's 12 px shift - shift tolerance remains the CNN's job, exactly as exp 6's probe found for survey-to-survey matching). Mechanism: a training-only decoder per member (two 3x3 convs with 2x upsampling, ~84k parameters, discarded before export) takes that member's 8x8x112 trunk feature map of its augmented own-survey view and must repaint the composite crop of the same position and heading at 32x32 (4 m/px), standardised per crop per channel so exposure and colour balance are not part of the target; MSE against it is added to the member's loss at weight 3. Each of the 64 feature cells then has to carry the stable coarse structure of its own 16 px patch (inside its 31 px receptive field - exp 5's 'bag of 31 m texture patches' becomes a bag of canonical-structure patches) and is paid nothing for carrying the survey-specific content the median removed; the pooled vector the cell head reads is a sum of exactly those descriptors. This is the library's L1-B (training-only reconstruction auxiliary, 'lives entirely in the never-flies lane') and L2's rule (predict a target that does not move; every expensive part is scaffolding dropped before export), re-aimed from lighting canonicalisation to survey canonicalisation, and it is the four-area era's exps 23/24/43 (redraw-the-clean-daytime-crop auxiliaries, verdicts void, measured on never-seen ground under a median metric) given a target that only this era's data asset makes possible: there was one photograph per place then, and a median needs three. It differs from exp 6 (blends as INPUTS: ghosted, physically meaningless frames the model had to classify) in that the composite is a TARGET and the inputs stay real photographs; from exp 8 in that the target is an image a two-layer decoder can certainly paint from 112-d local features, not a foundation model's semantics; and from exps 3/9 in that a fixed pixel-space target has no vacuous optimum (chance MSE is 1.0 by construction) and no collapsed one (a constant prediction scores exactly chance). The deployed graph is unchanged byte-for-byte (3,942,411 bytes).
